segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹמֵר: ״אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי בְּנִי בְּכוֹר לֹא יִטּוֹל פִּי שְׁנַיִם״; ״אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי בְּנִי לֹא יִירַשׁ עִם אֶחָיו״ – לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם, שֶׁהִתְנָה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In a case of «one who says: So-and-so, my firstborn son, will not take a double» portion of my estate; or one who says: «So-and-so, my son, will not inherit» my estate «among his brothers, he has said nothing, as he has stipulated counter to that which is written in the Torah.»

segments.he: הַמְחַלֵּק נְכָסָיו עַל פִּיו; רִיבָּה לְאֶחָד וּמִיעֵט לְאֶחָד, וְהִשְׁוָה לָהֶן אֶת הַבְּכוֹר – דְּבָרָיו קַיָּימִין. וְאִם אָמַר מִשּׁוּם יְרוּשָּׁה – לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם. כָּתַב בֵּין בַּתְּחִלָּה בֵּין בָּאֶמְצַע בֵּין בַּסּוֹף – מִשּׁוּם מַתָּנָה, דְּבָרָיו קַיָּימִין.
segments.en: With regard to «one» on his deathbed «who apportions his property orally,» granting it to his sons as a gift, and he «increased» the portion given «to one» of his sons «and reduced» the portion given «to one» son, «or equated» the portion of «the firstborn to» the portions of the other sons, «his statement stands. But if he said» that they will receive the property not as a gift but «as inheritance, he has said nothing.» If he «wrote» in his will, «whether at the beginning, or in the middle, or at the end,» that he is granting them the property «as a gift, his statement stands.»

moves.summary: Stipulation against Torah inheritance is void
Oral apportioning with more or less to each stands

positions.claim: stipulating that a firstborn not take double or a son not inherit is void; apportioning as a gift is valid, but 'as inheritance' is void
